runs.text: Egypt isn't called Egypt. Egyptians say <<ˈ|m|ɑ|s|r>>. Hebrew has <<m|ɪ|t|s|ˈ|r|ɑ|j|ɪ|m>>, from the same old root. Egypt comes from Greek. Fly west. Morocco is <<ɑ|l|ˈ|m|ɑ|g|r|ɪ|b>>: the west, where the sun sets. Algeria is <<ɑ|l|dʒ|æ|ˈ|z|ɑː|i|r>>. The islands, after the islets off Algiers. Way down south, Swaziland renamed itself <<ˌ|ɛ|s|w|ɑ|ˈ|t|iː|n|i>> in twenty eighteen. Turkey asked the UN to say <<t|ʊ|r|k|i|ˈ|j|eɪ>> in twenty twenty two. Persia? Iranians always said Iran. In nineteen thirty five, they asked the world to say it too. Jordan is <<ɑ|l|ɔ|r|ˈ|d|uː|n>>. Lebanon is <<l|ʊ|b|ˈ|n|ɑː|n>>, from an old word for white: the snow on its mountains. And Israel is <<j|ɪ|s|r|ɑ|ˈ|ɛ|l>>. In Genesis, it's the name given to Jacob, often read as: he struggles with God. Which one did you already know? Part three flies to Asia. Until then, remember:
